FINDING_ID: Codex_R3_FSM_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41  
DESCRIPTION: `max_rounds=1` is accepted by config, but the FSM cannot represent that case correctly. `max_round_idx` becomes `0`, yet `transition(Event.COMPLETE)` from `SYNTH` still creates `ROUND_1`. That state is outside the documented state set `{BLIND, SYNTH, ROUND_1, ..., ROUND_{N-1}, TERMINAL}` for `N=1`, and once entered it has no `COMPLETE` or `MAX` event available, only `CONVERGED`/`DIMINISHED`/`FAIL_CRITICAL`. I verified this at runtime: with `DynamicManagementConfig(max_rounds=1)`, the machine reaches `ROUND_1` and `valid_events()` there is `['sigma_fail_critical', 'sigma_converged', 'sigma_diminished']`. This breaks the claimed bounded linear progression and also makes `validate_no_failures()` invalid for a config the module currently permits.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either enforce `max_rounds >= 2` in `DynamicManagementConfig.__post_init__`, or explicitly support one-round mode by changing `valid_events()`/`transition()` so `SYNTH` does not emit `COMPLETE -> ROUND_1` when `max_round_idx == 0` and instead terminates via `MAX` or a dedicated one-round terminal path.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R3_FSM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.58  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47  
DESCRIPTION: `select_event()` does not honor the absorbing-state invariant. After the FSM is terminal, `select_event(round_complete=True, ...)` still returns `Event.COMPLETE`, and `select_event(critical_failure=True, ...)` still returns `Event.FAIL_CRITICAL`, even though `valid_events()` correctly returns `[]` in terminal state. I verified this at runtime by terminating the FSM with `FAIL_CRITICAL` and then calling `select_event()`: it returned real events instead of rejecting the call. That makes `select_event()` semantically inconsistent with both `valid_events()` and `transition()`, and it can mislead any caller that treats `select_event()` as the safe preflight for the next action.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add an early terminal guard in `select_event()` matching `transition()` (`raise RuntimeError` or `ValueError` if `self.is_terminal`), and/or derive the answer strictly from `valid_events()` so no event can be returned once the machine is absorbing.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: Codex_R3_FSM_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.73  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.70  
DESCRIPTION: The FSM’s `current_round` is not a stable round index for the rest of the system. It stays `0` in both `BLIND` and `SYNTH`, then only advances on `SYNTH -> ROUND_1` and later `ROUND_k -> ROUND_{k+1}` transitions. The manager already contains a workaround comment and a separate `_process_round_count` because `fsm.current_round` “gives the previous round's index” during `process_round()`, but other paths still use `self.fsm.current_round` directly. I verified the leak in `check_dispatch_feasibility()`: a blocked dispatch in `BLIND` and another blocked dispatch after advancing to `SYNTH` are both emitted and recorded with `round_idx=0`. This is a verified cross-component interface defect from the FSM API: event logs and any round-indexed monitoring built on `fsm.current_round` can collapse distinct phases into the same round or drift from detector histories keyed by `_process_round_count`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Define one authoritative round/phase index and use it everywhere. The simplest options are:  
1. Make `current_round` monotone across every dispatchable phase, including `SYNTH`, and remove `_process_round_count`; or  
2. Rename the FSM field to something narrower like `iterative_round_idx`, add a separate monotone `phase_idx`, and update manager/event code to use that authoritative counter for all emitted `round_idx` values.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

These are the new confirmed Round Progression findings from this slice; I did not promote weaker suspicions without stronger evidence.
